spreads.scene: A vast emerald jungle interior seen wide from the trail, exactly the world of the locked establishing plate: giant leaves, buttress roots, hanging lianas, warm shafts of morning light dropping through the canopy onto a narrow hand-cut trail that winds away into layered green depth. Far along the trail, three tiny anonymous travelers with packs walk away from the camera, small as beads, swallowed by the scale of the trees. The jungle is alive and generous with light, never gloomy. Keep the lower right of the frame calm: ferns and soft trail light only. The canopy is CLOSED overhead: no sky, no floating island, nothing above but leaves and light shafts. The island has not been introduced yet and must not appear.
negatives: the floating island or any floating rock visible anywhere in the sky or canopy break
any break in the canopy showing sky
spreads._caption: There is a jungle where the hopeful go. It is green and loud and alive, and it does not care how good your plan is. Everyone who walks in is looking for the same thing: a way up.

spreads.scene: From a small clearing in the jungle, the view opens upward: the canopy parts like a green window, and high in the warm open sky floats the island, exactly as the locked establishing plate paints it: a gentle teardrop of pale rock trailing thin mist, terraced gardens and low cream buildings on top, slender brass wind-spires catching the light. It is far, high, and unreachable; birds near it read as specks. At the clearing's edge, low in the left of frame, two anonymous travelers stand small with their backs to the camera, looking up at it. The lower right of the frame stays calm: leaves and soft light.
spreads._caption: Up is an island in the sky. It floats above the canopy in plain view, near enough to see its gardens and its bright machines, too far for any tree to reach. The people below call it Founder Paradise. Nobody steers it, not even the founders who made it up. It drifts where it drifts, and the winners ride along.

spreads.scene: One anonymous traveler is the moving subject: seen from the side at mid-distance, a wiry traveler with a pack and a machete strides from camera-right toward camera-left along a green trail, eyes fixed ahead on the trail, mid-swing clearing a frond. Directly behind and beside the trail, at arm's length from the traveler, the portal stands HIDDEN exactly as its locked hidden plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval only barely present as thin warm slivers of gold light behind hanging vines, broad leaves and leaf-shadow, its glow reaching no farther than the nearest leaves. The traveler does not see it and is walking past it. Ordinary jungle daylight everywhere else; the hiding is done by leaves, not gloom. Composition: the veiled portal stands left-of-center in the vine wall, the traveler passing through the right half, and the lower right corner stays calm ferns and trail for the caption card.
spreads._caption: There is one way up. Each era, one portal opens somewhere in the jungle: a tall door of warm light standing in the green. The jungle hides it the way it hides everything. You can cut a trail past it at arm's length and never know.
spreads.anonymous: one wiry anonymous traveler with a pack and a machete, passing without seeing
negatives: a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
the portal fully visible or unveiled (only thin warm slivers show through the leaves)

spreads.scene: A close, reverent study of the portal found and open, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval of warm golden light standing in a small jungle clearing, soft ink-wash edge with its thin brighter rim, a few small gold motes drifting, vines drawn aside like a curtain, its lower tip floating a hand's width above the ferns, warm light spilling softly onto the forest floor. Through the opening: warm gold light and a suggestion of open sky only. One anonymous founder, small against the portal's two-person height, is caught mid-step INTO the light at its left edge, silhouetted warm, pack still on their back; a second anonymous founder waits two steps behind on the trail at the lower left, next in line. The portal fills the left-of-center of the frame and stands well clear of the exact middle; the lower right quarter is calm ferns and warm-lit trail for the caption card.
negatives: a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
crowds or queues (two founders only)
a frame, ring or machinery around the light
spreads._caption: A portal starts wide enough for anyone who finds it. But every founder who steps through leaves it a little smaller, and every day it stands open it shrinks a little more, until one day it closes for good. The hopefuls call the time it is open a window. Rumor says the windows close faster every time.
spreads.anonymous: two anonymous founders: one silhouetted mid-step into the light, one waiting two steps behind

spreads.scene: A small gathering of people is the subject: at dusk, SEVEN anonymous hopefuls of mixed ages sit and stand in a loose half-circle around the closed portal exactly as its locked closed plate paints it: a flat quiet ring of pale gold blossoms on the forest floor, moss and soft ferns grown back inside it, a few small flat unmarked stones at its edge. No portal light anywhere; the scene is lit by one hooded lantern set on the ground and the last blue-green dusk in the leaves. One elder hopeful stands mid-story with both arms spread wide and high, telling it BIGGER than the ring at his feet; the listeners' faces are warm, tired and rapt. Nothing ominous: a campfire-story mood, kind and a little wistful. The blossom ring sits right-of-center with the gathering wrapped around its left; the lower right corner above the caption card stays calm ground and lantern glow.
spreads._caption: When a portal closes, it leaves a ring of pale gold flowers where the light once stood. The people who missed it gather there and tell stories about the ones who stepped through in time. The stories grow taller every season. That is how myths get written: by the people still on the ground.
spreads.anonymous: seven anonymous hopefuls of mixed ages, one elder mid-story with arms spread wide
negatives: a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
any portal light or glow from the blossom ring
ghost, spirit or supernatural glow above the ring

spreads.scene: The frame is the sky itself: high above the jungle canopy, which reads as a soft green sea along the bottom of the frame, THREE small pale-wood crates drift down under small round cream parachutes of plain cloth, at different depths and heights, cords taut, the farthest a tiny speck against warm morning cloud. In the lower left, one canopy gap opens to the forest floor, where a fourth crate has already landed and sits pried open in the ferns exactly as the compass's crated reference paints it: straw packing, and inside, the orange compass reading as one bright coin of clay orange, its short braided cream cord spilling over the crate's edge. NO lettering, stencil or logo on any crate, chute or the compass face. Composition: parachutes stepped across the upper right and middle sky, the opened crate small in the lower left gap; the bottom-right region stays soft canopy for the caption.
negatives: people or figures anywhere in this image
the floating island in frame
lettering, stencils, numbers or logos on any crate, parachute or compass
an antique compass-rose, star, tick marks, letters or numbers on any compass face (each face is plain cream with ONE dark orange-tipped needle only)
brass-only or gold-only compass shells (every compass shell is burnt-clay ORANGE enamel with only a thin brass rim)
military, cargo or supply-drop vocabulary (no pallets, no netting, no aircraft in frame)
spreads._caption: The founders up top tell stories too, and send them down. The pages fall a long way, and they land smudged into advice that points at nothing. So the island's keepers send something surer. Small crates drift down under parachutes, and inside each one is a smart orange compass whose needle always swings toward the live portal. The keepers want as many through as they can get. Rumor says the ones holding a sky-compass find the portal long before anyone else.

spreads.scene: Maya is the subject and fills the left half of the frame, mid-stride toward the camera-right along a dim pre-dawn trail, caught mid-swing clearing a hanging vine with a machete in her right hand, her closed silver laptop under her left arm as always, a small pack on her back. Her face is set with cheerful determination, jaw forward, eyes on the trail. The jungle around her is still night-blue and green, with the first warm light just reaching the leaves behind her. Her head reads about a third of the frame height: close enough to feel the effort. Sweat at her temple, leaves caught on her blazer sleeve. Keep the lower right calm: dim trail and ferns.
spreads._caption: Maya works harder than anyone in the jungle. She is up before the light, she carries her work everywhere, and she clears more trail in a week than most camps clear in a season. Hard work is her plan. She is sure it is enough.

spreads.scene: Maya stands small in the lower left, seen from three-quarters BEHIND, her head and body pointed the same way: toward the place the myth promised, in morning light before her: the closed portal exactly as its locked closed plate paints it, a flat quiet ring of pale gold blossoms on the forest floor, moss and ferns grown back inside, small flat unmarked stones at its edge, worn ground where years of visitors have stood. No portal light anywhere in the image. Her shoulders have just dropped; the machete hangs loose in her right hand; in her left hand, at her side, a worn folded myth-page with soft suggested (unreadable) lines. Morning light through the canopy falls gently on the blossom ring, which sits right-of-center at middle distance; the mood is quiet disappointment without any horror, a found grave of a door that was real. Lower right corner above the caption card stays calm ferns and path.
negatives: Maya's face in more than sliver profile
readable letters on the page
a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
any portal light or glow from the blossom ring
spreads._caption: She follows the most famous myth in the jungle to the place where a great portal once stood. It is exactly where the story said: a quiet ring of pale gold flowers in the green. It has been closed for years. The myth was true. It was just finished.

spreads.scene: A vast crowd is the ground of the image: an enormous sea of anonymous followers fills a broad jungle clearing from edge to edge, faces small and varied, packs and hats and hopeful upturned chins, stretching back until they blur into the green. Above them, on a tall grey rock outcrop rising at the left of frame, stands THE PROPHET exactly as his locked sheet paints him: silver hair, short white beard, long pale cream traveling coat, staff with its small brass bell in one hand, his polished brass speaking-trumpet raised to his lips with the other, mid-announcement, warm and certain. His figure reads about a quarter of the frame height. The crowd is already turning to run in the direction he points. Nobody in this image is lying and everybody is too late.
spreads._caption: One day a famous prophet arrives, and a million followers arrive behind him. He climbs the tallest rock and announces the portal's location to everyone at once. He is not lying. But a portal shrinks with every founder who passes through, and by the time anything can be announced to a million people, this one has shrunk too small for a crowd. Broadcast means too late.

spreads.scene: Night. Maya sits small in the lower left at a tiny camp: a low fire, a bedroll, her closed laptop on her knees under her folded hands, firelight warm on her thinking face. Above and to the right, filling most of the frame, floats one large SOFT PAINTED THOUGHT BUBBLE with a gently scalloped edge, its interior a warm cream vignette: inside it, two anonymous founders stand close together in painterly softness, one leaning to the other's ear, hand cupped, whispering, while pointing toward a tiny warm glow between distant painted trees. The bubble's content is the answer she is arriving at: not a myth, not a stage, a friend leaning close. The fire keeps the lower left warm; the lower right stays calm dark ferns.
spreads._caption: That night Maya counts every founder she has ever known who made it up. Not one of them found their portal in a myth or an announcement. Each one had a friend who found it and told them first, quietly, the same hour. Finders tell their friends.

spreads.scene: Three friends close around a map, seen CLOSE: the camera sits just over the ENGINEER's near shoulder in the lower right foreground, his charcoal-hooded back and shoulder softly out of focus and cropped by the frame, his lap and legs outside the picture. Across from him, sharp and warmly lit by a lantern set on a crate, MAYA leans in on the left pointing at the map, and CHRISSY, mid-laugh in the middle, presses a small pencil cross onto it. The map between them is hand-drawn: trail lines, small crosses for dead ends, a few pencil circles, NO readable words. Resting on the map near Maya's pointing hand sits one SMALL round pocket compass exactly as the locked prop paints it: burnt-clay orange enamel shell, thin brass rim, short braided cream cord, plain cream face with a single dark orange-tipped needle, no letters or marks on it. Evening jungle behind them is soft dark green bokeh. Three people, one lantern, one honest map.
negatives: readable letters, words or numbers on the map
the engineer's face or chest visible in the near foreground
spreads._caption: So she stops searching alone. She finds Chrissy, who lights up when she has something to share, and the engineer, who says plainly what he knows and what he does not. They draw their maps honestly, dead ends and all. A compass from the sky sits on the map where all three can read it, and they keep one rule: whoever finds it tells the others first.

spreads.scene: Chrissy is the subject, caught in the exact second of the find: she stands at the right of frame with one arm still holding back a heavy curtain of vines, and behind the parted green the portal stands found and open exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval of warm golden light, thin brighter rim, small gold motes, lower tip floating above the ferns, warm gold spilling onto the mossy floor. Through the opening: warm light and a hint of sky only. On its short braided cream cord around her neck, the orange compass rests at her collarbone, its dark needle pointing straight at the light. But Chrissy's body is already turning back toward camera-left, one foot pivoted, face lit half by portal-gold and half by trail-green, mouth opening into the grin of someone about to run and tell. The portal occupies the right third; her turning figure carries the middle-left; the lower left corner stays calm trail. Caption pos is top, so the upper band stays simple canopy shadow.
spreads._caption: It is Chrissy who finds it, on an ordinary morning, where the needle pointed, behind a curtain of vines she almost did not pull back. She does not climb a rock. She does not gather a crowd. She turns around and goes to get her friends.

the floating island visible through the opening (warm light and a hint of sky only here)
an antique compass-rose, star, points, tick marks, letters or numbers on the compass face (the face is plain warm cream with ONE dark clay-tipped needle only)

spreads.scene: The portal stands open in the green, left-of-center and clear of the exact middle of the frame, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval of warm golden light, vines drawn aside, lower tip floating above the ferns. THROUGH its opening, asked for by name: open morning sky and FOUNDER PARADISE, small and far and sunlit, exactly the silhouette of its locked establishing plate (teardrop of pale rock below, terraced gardens, low cream buildings, slender brass wind-spires), rising into view like a sunrise seen through a window. The island appears ONLY inside the portal's opening, never in the jungle sky. From the right, MAYA, CHRISSY and the ENGINEER walk together toward the light, seen from three-quarters BEHIND, Chrissy a half-step ahead with the warm gold already on her shoulders, Maya with her laptop under her arm, the engineer last with his steady stride; the portal is comfortably taller and wider than all three, room to spare. Warm gold spills over the trail toward them. The lower right corner above the caption card stays calm ferns and warm-lit trail.
spreads._caption: The portal is warm as a doorway at dusk, and it is still wide enough for every friend who comes. They step through together, out of the green and into the sky, and Founder Paradise comes up like a sunrise.
negatives: a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
the island anywhere OUTSIDE the portal's opening
a silver ribbon, thread, cable or elevator anywhere
the characters' faces in more than three-quarter-behind profile

spreads.scene: Three friends arrive: MAYA, CHRISSY and the ENGINEER walk away from the camera along the rim garden terrace of the island, exactly the terrace the locked plate paints: pale stone underfoot, the low rim rail on the right with open sky and the green sea of jungle far below, terraced gardens and low cream buildings rising on the left, a brass wind-spire against the warm sky. They are seen from BEHIND at mid-distance, heads and bodies pointed the same way, walking into their arrival; Maya's laptop is under her left arm even here. Coming the other way, two anonymous residents pause to welcome them, each holding a small folded hand-drawn map, marks visible as soft pencil lines only. The picture is warm, quiet and slightly smaller than a myth. Keep the lower right calm: rail and sky.
spreads._caption: Founder Paradise is smaller than the myths and kinder than the smudged advice. And nearly everyone who stands there arrived the same way: holding a map a friend drew.

spreads.scene: Maya alone at the rim: she stands at the low stone rail of the terrace, seen from three-quarters BEHIND at medium distance on the left of frame, head and torso pointed the same way, out and down toward the green sea of jungle far below. Her right hand has just opened: one crisp WHITE page slips from it into the bright air below the rail, caught by the light, its small neat writing suggested by soft fine lines that are not readable at this distance. The page is falling toward the world she came from, and it is not smudged. Her laptop rests on the rail under her left hand, and held gently against the laptop's lid by that same left hand sits her SMALL round pocket compass exactly as the locked prop paints it: burnt-clay orange enamel shell, thin brass rim, short braided cream cord trailing over the rail, plain cream face, single dark orange-tipped needle, no letters or marks on it. The terrace behind her is quiet gold; the jungle below is soft and far. Keep the lower right calm: open sky and the falling page's empty air. CRITICAL GEOGRAPHY: Maya is STANDING ON the one floating island; therefore NO island, rock or city may appear in the sky. The sky beyond the rail is empty warm air and soft cloud, and far below lies only the flat green sea of jungle.
negatives: readable letters, words or numbers on the page

a floating island, floating rock or city anywhere in the sky
any landmass in the sky
spreads._caption: Maya remembers the pages that fall and smudge. So she writes her story plainly and checks every word before she sends it down. I worked hard, and hard work was not enough. I held a compass from the sky, and a friend found the way and told me first. Work hard. Hold your compass. Find the friends who would tell you. Be one back.

spreads.scene: One young hopeful is the subject: in the first warm light of morning on a jungle trail, an anonymous young traveler with a pack stands mid-stride at the left of frame, a crisp WHITE unsmudged page held loosely in one hand at her side (its writing soft suggested lines, never readable), her other hand raised chest-high holding the orange compass on its short cream cord, its dark clay-tipped needle swinging DECISIVELY toward camera-right. Her face is turned the same way the needle points: alert, hopeful, mid-search, already moving. Deep in the green at the far right of frame, at mid-height and mostly veiled, the portal shows exactly as its locked hidden plate paints it: a few thin warm slivers of gold light behind hanging vines and leaf-shadow, far off but unmistakably alive. Dawn mist low on the trail, first sun catching the leaves; the mood is urgency with warmth, real hope, never dread: she is going to find it. The lower right corner above the caption card stays calm mist and ferns; the warm slivers sit above that band.

spreads._caption: Somewhere below, a hopeful reads a page that finally says what happened, and the needle of her sky-compass swings. This era's portal is open right now. Rumor says it opened wider than any portal before it. Rumor says it is closing faster than any portal has closed. So work hard. Hold your compass. Find the friends who would tell you first, and be one back. And from above, tell it straight. The light is standing somewhere in the green. Keep looking.
spreads.anonymous: one anonymous young hopeful with a pack, mid-stride, holding the page and the compass
